label: Late copy-phase steps (t>=11) with fed-back input in {d,n,a,k,w,o,2,c,i}
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires almost only in the copy phase (99.9% of mass). It never fires during the original phase and almost never at the delimiter or on recall_idx 0-1. Firing rises with absolute step: near zero before t=10, about 24% of steps at t>=12, so it is concentrated in long sequences (L=7-9). Input-token identity modulates it strongly: fed-back inputs d, n, a, k, w, o, 2, c, i have elevated rates (d about 4.9x lift), while v, l, u rarely fire. The output token has a weaker effect (c, a, n, y highest). Active steps tend to come in contiguous runs over several copy steps, and the runs break unpredictably. Neither prev_tok nor out_tok explained the breaks. Predicate (copy phase, t>=11, in_tok in the favoured set) gets dev F1 0.64 and mass recall 0.81. Recall is higher for stronger activations (the top quartile is better covered). Many steps that match the predicate are still inactive, so the token set is only a partial account of its token selectivity.
